readerTitle: Your best quarter can hide your next bad one
caseNote: 가상 사례 (회사 내 영업팀, 물류창고) + 실제 관찰 (산업안전 분야의 선행·후행 지표 구분) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 결과 숫자는 이미 지나간 일을 알려 줄 뿐이다. 결과보다 먼저 움직이는 숫자를 봐야 손쓸 시간이 생긴다.
misconception: 이번 분기 실적이 좋으면 다음 분기도 괜찮다. 가장 중요한 결과 숫자를 자주 보면 문제를 일찍 잡을 수 있다.

sources.text: 관리·성과측정 분야의 표준 개념 (선행 지표와 후행 지표)
OSHA, Using Leading Indicators to Improve Safety and Health Outcomes (2019)
영업팀·창고 수치는 모두 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 영업팀 수치는 가상입니다. 첫 미팅의 약 25%가 약 3개월 뒤 계약으로 이어진다는 가정입니다. 4월 계약 ≈ 1월 미팅 40 × 0.25 = 10, 5월 ≈ 2월 38 × 0.25 = 9.5(9로 표기), 6월 ≈ 3월 31 × 0.25 = 7.75(8로 표기), 7월 예상 ≈ 4월 26 × 0.25 = 6.5. 1~3월 계약(10, 10, 10)은 전년 10~12월 미팅이 약 40건이었다는 가정입니다.
산업안전 분야에서 재해율을 후행 지표로, 아차사고 보고와 안전점검 완료율을 선행 지표로 쓰는 구분은 널리 쓰입니다. OSHA 자료의 제목과 발행 연도는 게시 전에 확인하세요. 카드에는 구체적인 수치를 쓰지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Your best quarter can hide your next bad one
body: A regional sales team inside a large company closes its best first half in two years. Deals are on target every month. The director sends a thank-you email.
Three months later, the same team misses target badly. Nothing sudden happened. The warning had been sitting in a spreadsheet since March.

image.label: A celebration at the front, a falling line on a screen behind
image.brief: 사무실 장면. 앞쪽에서 팀원들이 케이크와 함께 축하하고 있고, 뒤쪽 모니터에 아무도 보지 않는 하강 곡선이 작게 떠 있음. 실제 회사 로고나 상표 없이.

cards.title: It's the end of June. What tells you about September?
body: You lead the team. Deals closed have hit target every month this year. Your boss asks how next quarter looks.
Which number would you check first?

options.text: Deals closed this quarter, compared with target
options.feedback: It's the number everyone is judged on, so it feels like the right one. But it tells you how the last few months went, not the next few.

options.text: First meetings booked with new prospects each month
options.feedback: Meetings today become deals months from now. If this number is falling, you can still act before it shows up in results.
It matters for revenue, and it can warn you about pricing pressure. But it says little about whether enough deals are coming at all.

cards.title: Meetings fell in March. Deals fell in June.
body: About a quarter of first meetings turn into deals roughly three months later. So deals in June reflect meetings in March.
By the time deals drop, the meetings that could have prevented it should have been booked months ago. July's deals will come from April's 26 meetings.

cards.title: Leading vs lagging indicators
body: A **lagging indicator** measures a result after it has happened: revenue, profit, on-time deliveries, customers lost.
A **leading indicator** measures something that moves *before* the result and helps predict it: meetings booked, orders in the pipeline, machines serviced on schedule.
Lagging numbers tell you whether you won. Leading numbers tell you whether you're about to.

image.label: A road with a warning sign ahead and a rear-view mirror
image.brief: 운전석 시점 일러스트. 앞 유리 너머 멀리 "Leading" 경고 표지판, 백미러 안에 "Lagging" 라벨이 붙은 지나온 길. 단순한 플랫 스타일.

cards.softwareNote: Revenue and churn (customers who cancel) are lagging. How many new users reach a key action in their first week often leads both by months, so many teams watch it weekly.

cards.title: Results get the attention. Causes get the time.
body: Lagging numbers are what bonuses, board meetings and targets are built on, so they get discussed most. But when a result moves, its cause is often months old.
A good leading indicator buys you that time back. It needs two things: a real link to the result you care about, and a short enough cycle that you can check it weekly and still react.

cards.title: Safety teams learned this early.
body: In workplace safety, injury rates are the classic lagging number. Waiting for injuries to rise before acting means someone has already been hurt.
So many safety programs also track leading numbers: near-miss reports, safety checks completed, training finished. These move before injuries do, and they point to what to fix.
The same split works for a factory line, a kitchen or a support desk.

image.label: Factory floor with a near-miss board on the wall
image.brief: 공장 바닥 장면. 벽에 "Near misses this week" 보드가 있고 작업자가 메모를 붙이고 있음. 한쪽 구석에 작은 "Days without injury" 표지판. 실제 기업 로고 없이.

cards.title: A leading indicator is a bet, not a fact.
body: Some early numbers move with the result by coincidence. Check that yours actually predicts the outcome over time before you steer by it.
And once a leading number becomes a target, people can push it without the result following. Reward meetings booked, and you may get lots of meetings with people who will never buy.
Keep watching the lagging number too. It's how you check that your early signal still means something.

cards.title: Now it's a warehouse.
body: You run a distribution warehouse. Last month, 97% of orders shipped on time, your best month this year. You want to catch the next problem before customers feel it.
Which number do you add to your daily check?

options.text: Orders still waiting to be picked after 24 hours, counted each morning
options.feedback: A growing backlog shows up days before late shipments do. It gives you time to move staff or add a shift.

options.text: The on-time rate, checked weekly instead of monthly
options.feedback: Faster feedback helps, but it's still a result. You learn about late orders only after they're already late.
It's an important signal, but it lags even more than the on-time rate. By the time complaints arrive, the damage is done.

cards.title: Results show where you've been. Leading numbers show where you're heading.
body: Pair every result you're judged on with one number that moves before it.
**Try it today:** take the number you check most often. If it's a result, find one earlier step that drives it, and start counting that step every week.
